result.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
result.summary: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapter requires only an image; textual references remain fixed. In zero-shot classification, CARET achieves 67.80\% accuracy on CheXpert 5$\times$200 and 65.20\% on RSNA. These scores exceed the published CLEFT-LoRA results by 1.06 and 0.27 percentage points, respectively. Comparisons to literature baselines are informative but not controlled for differences in pretraining and evaluation protocols. Ablations across eight components identify the four-state distinction and assertion objective as major contributors, with task-dependent effects for nonmention preservation and pair alignment.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CARET，一种参数高效的医学图像侧适配方法：保留预训练图像与文本编码器，用成对正负临床陈述构造低维语义校正空间，以有界残差调整图像特征，并监督区分「明确存在、否定、不确定、未提及」四种断言状态，在 CheXpert 5×200 与 RSNA 零样本分类上优于 CLEFT-LoRA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以有界残差沿语义方向编辑图像特征、并用断言状态监督避免无视觉依据的预测，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的视觉内容筛选与定向编辑提供方法线索；但该工作面向分类而非推理，校正方向是否真对应视觉证据需核查。
